summary: This was an open seat because Republican Sen. Tommy Tuberville ran for governor instead. Barry Moore (Republican) defeated Everett Wess (Democrat).

candidates.name: Barry Moore
candidates.bio: Barry Moore is a Republican U.S. representative from Alabama's 1st district and a member of the House Agriculture and Judiciary committees. Before Congress he started an industrial waste hauling company and served eight years in the Alabama House. He says he was the first elected official in America to back Donald Trump for president.

positions.summary: Says taxes will be lower when Alabamians file on April 15 and that gas prices and grocery bills are coming down.
Says immigrants in the country illegally who commit crimes must be deported and that the law must keep being enforced.
Says Medicaid and Medicare should remain available but no other taxpayer-funded programs are necessary.
Says he supports school choice, including voucher programs, tax credits, charter schools, private schools and home schools.
Says abortion providers, including Planned Parenthood, should not receive taxpayer funds, and that elective abortion should be allowed only in cases of rape, incest or the life of the mother.

candidates.name: Everett Wess
candidates.bio: Everett Wess is a Birmingham attorney and managing partner of The Wess Law Firm since 2001. He served as a Midfield municipal court judge for eight years and is state president of the Alabama New South Coalition.

positions.summary: Says economic opportunity is vital for Alabama's growth and prosperity.
Says affordable healthcare is essential, including funding for rural medical providers and support for hospitals in underserved areas.
Says Alabama must ensure quality public education to equip future leaders.
Said in June 2026 that immigration courts should be properly funded so people seeking legal status can have their cases resolved in a timely way.

factCheckNote: Winner matches AP-sourced tally (political.org Nov 14 tally, AP called 34 of 35). Certified count: pages of the Alabama Secretary of State canvassing PDF are marked "Certified by the State Canvassing Board November 23, 2026". Shares include write-ins in the total.
